title: Former Director of Data Science at Meta Believes Advantage+ and Outcome-Focused Measurement Are Durable Advertising Advantages
expert: Former Director of Data Science at Meta (led ~50 data scientists on ads delivery and Advantage+); now at another company; interview 2026-10-22
verdict: A former Meta data-science director says a 10% gain in value-weighted conversions translated into ~10% advertiser revenue over 3–10 months, supporting Advantage+ durability, while Europe ad growth reportedly slowed to 18% in Q3 from 40% in Q1 (hearsay).

Ad price per ad + impression growth: 10% more value-weighted conversions → 10% more revenue over 3–10 months (from tenure); fits 3Q26 GEM gains of +9.6% app-ad conversions (SB #65096). → Tenet 1 (core ads) ↑
Europe ad growth 18% in Q3 vs 40% in Q1 (hearsay) vs total 3Q26 revenue +26% (SB #61735): Europe lagging. → Tenet 1 (core ads) ↓
Muse/agent monetization: agent fees such as 1% on a $6,000 insurance saving (hypothetical); Oppenheimer found only 19% of consumers would pay for an agent (SB #51221). → Tenet 3 (Muse $5B+) →

changes: 10% conversion → 10% revenue link vs 3Q26 GEM +9.6% app-ad conversions and +1.7% off-site (SB #65096): consistent (conversion gains feed revenue).
Europe ad growth 18% in Q3 (hearsay) vs total 3Q26 revenue +26%, price per ad +14% (SB #61735): Europe below group.
Agent monetization via transaction fees (hypothetical) vs Oppenheimer survey: 19% would pay for an AI agent (SB #51221): unresolved.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (core ads): ↑ — conversion gains convert ~1:1 to revenue over 3–10 months; offset by Europe 18% vs 40% (hearsay).
Tenet 3 (Muse $5B+): → — monetization models are hypothetical (1% transaction fee); 2–3 agent winners expected.
